clue.text: Glorious rendition of Unter den Linden?

parts.note: German unter means under, and sub is the Latin prefix for under
German Linden are lime trees; den is just 'the'

explanation.surface: Is a performance of a tune about Berlin's famous boulevard glorious?
explanation.walkthrough: Unter den Linden is the grand avenue in Berlin; translated word by word it gives under-the-lime, and SUB (under) + LIME makes a word for glorious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sublime is of such excellence or grandeur that it inspires awe.

clue.text: Europa, for example, is in position as a state

explanation.surface: A moon of Jupiter reckoned to be ranked as a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Europa is a moon of Jupiter; a dependent country under a larger power is called a satellite state.
explanation.definitionFit: Europa is a moon orbiting Jupiter, and a country under the sway of a bigger power holds that subordinate position.

clue.text: Shoes with black heels

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a heel is an old word for a cad, so heels are rogues

explanation.surface: Footwear with dark heels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heels' looks like part of the shoe but means scoundrels.
explanation.definitionFit: Brogues are stout leather shoes with decorative perforations.

clue.text: Tense and immature

explanation.surface: Nervous and childish.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperfect is a grammatical tense for continuing past action, and something not fully formed is incomplete or immature.

clue.text: Sin of diplomat the circle rejected?

indicators.note: rejected says the round letter is thrown out of the word for a diplomat

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomatic messenger
O is round like a circle

explanation.surface: Which sin made a diplomat shunned by his social set?
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: River board responsible for what is safe for the consumer

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
a table is a board, as in 'bed and board'

explanation.surface: A water authority takes charge of what may safely be drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Potable water is fit to drink, so safe for someone consuming it.

clue.text: Mournful line, meant to reform when in prison cell

indicators.note: in says the rearranged word is placed within the cell

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a prison cell

indicators.note: to reform means to form again, so the letters of meant are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sad line about a reformed character serving time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges MEANT into NTAME, placed in PETER. The pentameter is the second line of the elegiac couplet, used for laments.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac verse, the poetry of lament, alternates hexameters with five-foot lines.

clue.text: Tax note about smash-hit

indicators.note: about says the note goes around the scrambled word

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: smash breaks the word hit into a new order

explanation.surface: A levy on the profits from a big hit record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smash-hit' reads as a success; 'smash' rearranges HIT into ITH, which TE goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of produce paid as a levy to the church.

clue.text: Dipping is fine, almost sure to succeed?

annotationWithheld.why: Dipping is fine, almost sure to succeed? (7): BATHING; no sound parse found for 'is fine, almost sure to succeed' (B + A THING?), and no blog or database gives one
annotationWithheld.clue: Dipping is fine, almost sure to succeed?

clue.text: Bond-man whose clients are numbered

parts.note: not a spy but the machine that draws winning British Premium Bond numbers, whose holders are known only by number

explanation.walkthrough: Premium Bonds are a UK government savings lottery; the random-number machine picking the winners has a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment selects winning Premium Bond numbers.

clue.text: Hamlet, though shortened, has the King and the prince

indicators.note: shortened says the word though loses its tail, as in the informal written form

parts.note: taken as written before cutting
R, for Rex, is the usual abbreviation for king
P is an abbreviation for prince

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's play, cut down, still has the king and the Danish prince in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' looks like the play, given the King and prince, but it is a small village. THO is the clipped spelling of THOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorp is an archaic word for a village or small settlement, which is a hamlet.

clue.text: Card-game for the majority of the French

explanation.surface: A gambling game suited to most French people.
explanation.walkthrough: Vingt-et-un is French for twenty-one, the age at which one used to come of age, that is reach one's majority.
explanation.definitionFit: The card game is a form of blackjack or pontoon, and twenty-one in French is the old age of legal adulthood.

clue.text: Liberal output of painter (not English) shown here?

indicators.note: not says a letter is to be left out of the painter's body of work

parts.note: an oeuvre is the complete body of an artist's work

explanation.surface: A liberal-minded painter's work, minus the English, put on display somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole clue read as a question: the Louvre in Paris is where a painter's output is shown.
explanation.definitionFit: The Louvre is the Paris museum where great paintings are exhibited.

clue.text: You may get a day out crossing this

definitions.text: You may get a day out crossing this

parts.words: You may get a day out crossing this
parts.note: not an outing but a calendar day lost or gained when travelling across a certain line in the Pacific

explanation.definitionFit: Crossing the International Date Line puts the traveller's calendar one day out.

clue.text: Mint coin of the realm

explanation.surface: A freshly minted royal coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' poses as new coinage but is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennyroyal is a herb of the mint family, and a royal penny would be the kingdom's coinage.

clue.text: Susie's spoilt children

indicators.note: spoilt signals that the letters of the name are damaged into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A girl called Susie has pampered, spoilt kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoilt' reads as describing the children, but it rearranges SUSIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal and formal word for offspring.

clue.text: Look wide-awake with Euphrasy

parts.note: to eye is to look at
bright means alert or wide-awake

explanation.surface: Seeming alert after treatment with a herbal remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphrasy is the botanical name for the meadow plant once used to treat sore eyes.

clue.text: Reports heard of its flight down under

definitions.text: Reports heard of its flight down under

parts.words: Reports heard of its flight down under
parts.note: the reports are gunshots, and a bird of Australia is named after a firearm

explanation.walkthrough: Down under means Australia; the bird's name was traditionally linked to the whirring sound of its wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Riflebirds are Australian birds of paradise, named for their gun-like wing noise.

clue.text: First coal shift to use eye protectors

indicators.note: shift says the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Miners on the first coal shift must wear goggles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a work shift in a mine, but it rearranges FIRST COAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Trifocals are spectacles with three lens zones that aid and guard the eyes.

clue.text: Roughly sixteen at church? Not much of a living!

indicators.note: roughly says the letters of sixteen are only approximately in order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England; at places it after the jumbled number

explanation.surface: A sixteen-year-old's life in church, scarcely worth calling a life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' looks like an approximate age and 'at church' a place of worship; the first signals a jumble, the second the Church of England's initials. 'Not much of a living' is a bare existence.
explanation.definitionFit: A bare existence is mere survival, barely amounting to a life or livelihood.

clue.text: Blasphemous to say I am pope?

indicators.note: to say signals that the words are spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: I'm Pius, one of the popes called Pius

explanation.surface: Would claiming the papacy for oneself be sacrilegious?
explanation.walkthrough: Pius is the name of twelve popes, so a pope might say I'm Pius.
explanation.definitionFit: Impious means lacking reverence for God, irreverent or profane.

clue.text: Falstaff ungirds, consuming mushrooms

indicators.note: consuming says the words eat up, and so contain, the answer letters

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's fat knight loosens his belt and eats mushrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: Falstaff, the fat knight of Shakespeare, would be a big eater, so 'consuming' looks like eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushrooms are a familiar kind of fungus, the plural matching.

clue.text: First officer over divers is offensive

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first piece above the second

parts.note: Number One, written No 1, is naval slang for the first lieutenant
divers is an old word for various or some

explanation.surface: The senior officer above the frogmen is objectionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' looks like underwater swimmers but is the old adjective meaning sundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means foul-smelling or disgusting, unpleasant to the senses.

clue.text: Boneless cabinet of earlier times?

parts.note: the nursery rhyme of Old Mother Hubbard, who went to fetch her dog a bone and found the storage cabinet bare

explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen storage cabinet with shelves, famously empty of bones in the old rhyme.

clue.text: Colonel we hear is an oil-producer, policeman and painter

definitions.text: Colonel we hear is an oil-producer

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman
RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: A list of jobs: army officer, police officer, artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel sounds like kernel; copra is dried coconut kernel pressed for oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Copra is the dried meat of the coconut, from which coconut oil is extracted.

clue.text: Water unsuitable for fragile canoe

indicators.note: fragile suggests the boat breaks apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rough seas are no place for a flimsy little boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is a vast body of salt water.

clue.text: Minor point in denouement of yarn

indicators.note: a denouement is an unravelling, so the letters of the fodder are unpicked and rewound

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A small detail in the ending of a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' poses as a story whose ending is a denouement; it is wool. 'in denouement of' unravels MINOR plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: Merino is a fine wool spun from the fleece of a breed of sheep.

clue.text: Softwood bargain

explanation.surface: Cheap pine timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is sawn fir or pine timber, and a deal is also an agreement or good buy.

clue.text: One converted to Presley accidentally?

indicators.note: accidentally says the letters fall into a new order by chance

explanation.surface: Someone who became an Elvis fan by chance.
explanation.definitionFit: A proselyte is a convert to a new faith or cause.

clue.text: False ideas of one having to make the rounds of American city

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to do the rounds is to make the rounds
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Misconceptions about a person touring an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: Idola, Francis Bacon's term, are the false notions or fallacies of the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Idola is Latin plural for phantoms, Bacon's name for fallacies that mislead thinking.

clue.text: Magazine for footballers

explanation.surface: A sports periodical aimed at players of soccer.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a store of weapons, like an ammunition magazine, and also the name of a famous London football club.

clue.text: Hierarchical structures of some boards?

explanation.surface: Ranked organisations seen in certain company boardrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: The board is a game board: Snakes and Ladders, the children's dice game.
explanation.definitionFit: Career ladders are ranked systems of promotion, and the game board in snakes-and-ladders features climbing ladders.
